clue.text: Baseball player, one getting walked all over?

definitions.text: Baseball player, one getting walked all over?

parts.words: Baseball player, one getting walked all over?
parts.note: the baseball player who throws to the batter, read playfully as a ground (a cricket or football field) that people tread across

explanation.surface: A baseball player is trampled by the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: a cricket or football field is something walked all over, and an extra ending makes it a person, the man on the mound in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the player who throws the ball at the batter from the mound has this title.

clue.text: Personal assistant being quick in clerical office

parts.note: pacy means fast

explanation.surface: An efficient secretary works in a church office.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope's position or term is the highest office in the Roman Catholic church.

clue.text: Ingeniously turn a pail into protective headgear

indicators.note: worked ingeniously, the letters are cleverly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bucket is cleverly made into a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides waterproof sheeting, the word is an old name for a sailor's tarred hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's waterproof hat of tarred cloth was once called by this name.

clue.text: Cut down docks, removing head and end of root

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: wharves are docks where ships load

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts back dock plants, taking off their tops and root tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docks' are weeds in the surface but quays here: WHARVES loses its head (W), then 'end of root' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather a crop is to reap or cut it down in the fields.

clue.text: Colour your label differently

indicators.note: arranged differently, the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone advises redesigning the colour of a label.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep bright shade associated with the British monarchy is a named tint.

clue.text: Puck introduced here — look away

parts.note: to face something is to look towards it
off means away, as in 'he's off'

explanation.surface: An ice-hockey commentator tells viewers to look away as play starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck is the ice-hockey disc, not Shakespeare's sprite: play begins when the referee drops it between two opposing players.
explanation.definitionFit: In ice hockey the restart where the referee drops the disc between two players is called by this name.

clue.text: Look in marshy area for criminal

indicators.note: one word is placed in the other

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A detective searches the marshes for an outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has committed a serious crime is a convict or wrongdoer.

clue.text: Showing competence, unfinished Picasso is kept in bank

indicators.note: something kept in another is held inside it

parts.note: a cay is a low sandbank or reef

indicators.note: an unfinished word loses its final letter

parts.note: Pablo was Picasso's first name

explanation.surface: An incomplete Picasso painting is stored in a bank vault, which shows good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; here it is a sandbank (CAY), and Picasso is reduced to his first name, PABLO, minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something skilfully and efficiently is acting with ability.

clue.text: Ring with a stone turned up in the end

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A ring set with a stone appears at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses A GEM to MEGA, which follows O.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the finish, as in 'alpha and omega'.

clue.text: One's regular turn to ensure machinery conserves power?

definitions.text: One's regular turn to ensure machinery conserves power?

parts.words: One's regular turn to ensure machinery conserves power?
parts.note: reads like a person's routine shift, but describes a heavy rotating disc that keeps an engine turning steadily by storing momentum

explanation.surface: Someone takes a regular shift making sure the machines save energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' suggests a person's spell of duty; it is a literal rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy rotating wheel stores kinetic energy and smooths out a machine's running.

clue.text: Description of beam incorporated in doorway

indicators.note: something incorporated in another thing is taken into its body, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a portal is a grand doorway or entrance
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: An architect describes a beam built into a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction or account of someone, in words or on stage, is a representation of them.

clue.text: American writer's unknown literary output

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer; the possessive gives his name plus S
Y is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Nobody knows what an American author actually wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry, especially old-fashioned or ornate verse, is a writer's literary work.

clue.text: Hound has gone into church

indicators.note: one word has gone into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A dog has wandered into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a noun, a dog, but it is a verb: to pursue.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to pursue them relentlessly.

clue.text: Coastal resort — Chesil Bank, for instance

definitions.meaning: a seaside city in southern California
Chesil Bank is an 18-mile shingle ridge on the Dorset coast in England, an example of a lengthy shore

explanation.surface: A seaside town is compared with a famous stretch of English shingle.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesil Bank (or Beach) runs about 18 miles along the Dorset coast of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian resort city has this name, and an extended stretch of shore is literally this.

clue.text: The shepherd — miniature version of Gainsborough's portrait?

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme boy told to come blow his horn because the sheep are in the meadow
Gainsborough painted The Blue Boy; a small edition of it would be a little one

explanation.surface: An art critic calls a pastoral painting a scaled-down Gainsborough.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gainsborough's famous portrait is The Blue Boy; the nursery rhyme's boy is a careless shepherd asleep under a haystack.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme child who minds sheep has this name, and it also describes a small copy of the painting.

clue.text: Liberal and I being a little sectarian

definitions.text: Liberal and I being a little sectarian

parts.words: Liberal and I being a little sectarian
parts.note: in Gulliver's Travels, the two warring sects split over which end of a boiled egg to break; one with the 'big' view opposes one who prefers the little end

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to being slightly partisan alongside a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift's Lilliputians fought over whether to open eggs at the big or little end; 'Liberal' (generous, big) and 'a little' point at the two factions.
explanation.definitionFit: In Swift's satire, members of the faction breaking eggs at the larger end are a sect.

clue.text: Here was relief for a woman, as the old story is told

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.words: a woman, as the old story
parts.note: a woman's legend: lady's myth

explanation.surface: A woman finds comfort in an old legend being retold.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladysmith, in South Africa, was besieged by the Boers and famously relieved in 1900; 'relief' means lifting a siege, not comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African town was besieged in the Boer War and its relief in 1900 was celebrated.

clue.text: Go out with girl to English or Welsh town

parts.note: the tide ebbs when it goes out
Val is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone leaves with a girlfriend for a town in England or Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A former mining town in south Wales, in Blaenau Gwent, has this name.

clue.text: Terrible nag folk banned The Old Lady

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful nag is barred by the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Lady of Threadneedle Street is the traditional nickname of Britain's central bank in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's central bank is nicknamed the Old Lady of Threadneedle Street after its London address.

clue.text: Exaggerated love composer bestowed on daughter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer
D is short for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A composer lavished too much affection on his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have overacted or taken something too far is to have gone to excess.

clue.text: Jack had wasted a little time, the rascal

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)

indicators.note: letters wasted are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: T is short for time

explanation.surface: A ne'er-do-well called Jack frittered away a bit of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' scrambles HAD to ADH.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned phrase for a scoundrel or rogue is this hat idiom.

clue.text: Saw red about finally getting taunted

indicators.note: one word about another goes around it

parts.note: to see red is to be furious, to rage

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone was furious when at last they were mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is past tense of see, not a cutting tool: saw red means raged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be teased or mocked is to have been ribbed, an old sense of ragging.

clue.text: Reduce the value of record

definitions.meaning: in accounting, to lower the book value of an asset

explanation.surface: An accountant lowers an asset's value and logs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Accountants lower an asset's book value this way, and to note something on paper is the same phrase.

clue.text: Which organ contains blood-like fluid?

indicators.note: the two words together contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A quiz asks which bodily organ holds a fluid like blood.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this ethereal fluid flowed in the veins of the gods.

clue.text: What convicts used to pick from tree, with some show of hesitation

parts.note: an oak is a tree
um is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Convicts picked something from a tree, hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Prisoners were once set to picking apart old tarred rope into loose fibre used to caulk ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose fibre from untwisted old rope was teased apart by prisoners for caulking seams.

clue.text: Where to find flounders floundering

definitions.meaning: flounders are flatfish, living in the ocean

explanation.surface: Flatfish are struggling about in their habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounders' is the fish, not the verb; then 'floundering' is the idiom for being bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish live in the ocean, and someone bewildered is figuratively lost in the ocean too.

clue.text: A degree — being without one is a pest

indicators.note: one word being outside another means it surrounds it

parts.note: a PhD is a doctoral degree
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone lacking a degree is called a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: PHD goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are small sap-sucking insects that damage garden plants.

clue.text: Honouring with honour coming round late in the day

indicators.note: one word coming round another surrounds it

parts.note: in card games such as bridge the king is one of the honour cards
night is the late part of the day

explanation.surface: Someone is given an award late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honour' is the card sense: in bridge the ace, king, queen, jack and ten are honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbing someone a Sir, with a sword on the shoulder, is a way of honouring them.

clue.text: Could this make me a lord?

definitions.text: Could this make me a lord?

indicators.note: asks whether these letters can be made into a new word, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ambitious man wonders what would turn him into a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: the letters of ME A LORD rearrange, and the rank asked about would indeed make one a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A count's rank or territory in the British peerage is one that makes its holder a peer.

clue.text: Nicked paper money outside church — a note

indicators.note: one word outside another goes round it

parts.note: a note is a piece of paper money
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone pinched banknotes from outside a church, leaving a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' is British slang for stolen, but here it means cut with small marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nicked has small V-shaped cuts in it.
